title: Get all items from repeated XML elements
prompt:
An XML order has multiple `<line>` elements inside. Extract an array of the text content of each line.

You must return **all** lines, not just the first one.

Bonus: also extract the order's `id` attribute and the `currency` of the first line.

Output a JSON object with keys `lines`, `orderId`, and `firstCurrency`.

cases.input:
<order id="ORD-004">
  <line currency="CAD">First</line>
  <line currency="CAD">Second</line>
  <line currency="CAD">Third</line>
  <line currency="CAD">Fourth</line>
  <line currency="CAD">Fifth</line>
</order>

hints: The `.` selector on a repeated element gives you only the **first** match. Use `.*` to get all of them.
On XML, `@name` reads an attribute. `payload.order.@id` pulls the `id` attribute from the `order` element.
Combine selectors: `payload.order.*line` returns an **array**, so you can use `map` or index it with `[0]`.
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  lines: payload.order.*line,
  orderId: payload.order.@id,
  firstCurrency: payload.order.*line[0].@currency
}

mustFail.why: uses . instead of .* so only gets the first line
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  lines: payload.order.line,
  orderId: payload.order.@id,
  firstCurrency: payload.order.line.@currency
}

explanation.approach: On XML with repeated elements, `.` silently returns only the first match. `.*` breaks that silence and returns all of them as an array. The `@` symbol reads attributes instead of child elements.

snippets.label: The answer
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{
  lines: payload.order.*line,
  orderId: payload.order.@id,
  firstCurrency: payload.order.*line[0].@currency
}
snippets.note: `.*line` is what makes the difference. Without the `*`, you get only the first.

snippets.label: Why . loses lines
snippets.note: Only the first line. The selector stops at the first match and returns its value, not an array. Perfect for single child, catastrophic for repeated ones.

snippets.label: Getting all lines with .*
snippets.note: The `*` makes it an array. Now you have all of them and can index or transform them as needed.

snippets.label: Reading attributes
snippets.note: `@` is the attribute syntax. `payload.order.@id` reads the `id` attribute of the `order` element.

snippets.label: Attribute on an array element
snippets.note: First get the array with `.*line`, then `map` over it and read `@currency` from each element.
